title: Psalms Chapter 129 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 129 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 129 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 129.

questions.question: What is the title or description given to Psalms 129:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:1 begins with 'A Song of degrees,' which is the title or description of the psalm.

questions.question: Who is encouraged to say, 'Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:1 ends with 'may Israel now say:' indicating that Israel is the one encouraged to say this.

questions.question: According to Psalms 129:2, what is true about the afflictions from youth?
options: They have not prevailed against me
They have been few in number
questions.correctAnswer: They have not prevailed against me
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:2 states, 'Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth: yet they have not prevailed against me.'

questions.question: What imagery is used in Psalms 129:3 to describe the affliction?
options: The plowers plowed upon my back
questions.correctAnswer: The plowers plowed upon my back
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:3 uses the imagery 'The plowers plowed upon my back: they made long their furrows' to describe affliction.

questions.question: According to Psalms 129:4, what has the LORD done to the cords of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:4 states, 'The LORD is righteous: he hath cut asunder the cords of the wicked.'

questions.question: Who are said to be confounded and turned back in Psalms 129:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:5 says, 'Let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Zion.'

questions.question: In Psalms 129:6, what are the enemies compared to?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:6 states, 'Let them be as the grass upon the housetops, which withereth afore it groweth up.'

questions.question: What happens to the grass on the housetops according to Psalms 129:6?
options: It withers before it grows up
questions.correctAnswer: It withers before it grows up
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:6 describes the grass as 'which withereth afore it groweth up.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 129:7, what does the mower not fill his hand with?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:7 says, 'Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand,' referring to the grass on the housetops.

questions.question: Who does not say, 'The blessing of the LORD be upon you' according to Psalms 129:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:8 states, 'Neither do they which go by say, The blessing of the LORD be upon you.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 129:2 says that the afflictions from youth ultimately prevailed against the speaker.
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:2 clearly states that though afflicted many times from youth, 'yet they have not prevailed against me.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 129:4, the LORD is righteous and has cut asunder the cords of the wicked.
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:4 states, 'The LORD is righteous: he hath cut asunder the cords of the wicked.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 129:5 prays that those who love Zion shall be confounded and turned back.
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:5 prays that 'Let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Zion,' not those who love Zion.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 129:8 mentions that those who pass by bless the people in the name of the LORD.
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:8 states the opposite: 'Neither do they which go by say, The blessing of the LORD be upon you.'

questions.question: In Psalms 129, which event is mentioned FIRST?
options: They afflicted me from my youth
The LORD cut asunder the cords of the wicked
Enemies are compared to grass upon housetops
The mower does not fill his hand
questions.correctAnswer: They afflicted me from my youth
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned is 'Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth' in Psalms 129:1.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 129 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 129 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 129:4, what has the LORD done to the cords of the wicked?
options: He hath cut asunder the cords of the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: He hath cut asunder the cords of the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:4 states that the LORD is righteous and has cut asunder the cords of the wicked, showing His power to break the bonds of evil.

questions.question: How does Psalms 129:5 describe the fate of those who hate Zion?
options: They shall prosper and be exalted
They shall be confounded and turned back
They shall be forgiven and embraced
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be confounded and turned back
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:5 specifically says that those who hate Zion shall be confounded and turned back, indicating God’s protection over Zion and judgment on its enemies.

questions.question: What does Psalms 129:6 compare the enemies of Zion to?
options: Grass upon the housetops which withereth before it groweth up
questions.correctAnswer: Grass upon the housetops which withereth before it groweth up
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:6 uses the simile of grass on housetops that wither before growing up to illustrate the fleeting and weak nature of those who oppose Zion.

questions.question: What practical lesson about trusting God can be drawn from Psalms 129:4 and 129:5?
options: Trust in human strength to overcome adversity
Trust that God will break the power of evil and protect His people
Trust that enemies will never be defeated
questions.correctAnswer: Trust that God will break the power of evil and protect His people
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 together teach that God, being righteous, cuts the cords of the wicked and causes those who hate Zion to be confounded and turned back, encouraging believers to trust in God's justice and protection.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 129:6 and 129:7, what is implied about the enemies’ productivity or success?
options: They will be fruitful and multiply
They will not yield a harvest nor fill the mower’s hand
questions.correctAnswer: They will not yield a harvest nor fill the mower’s hand
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 describe the enemies as grass that withereth before growing up, so the mower does not fill his hand nor the binder his bosom, implying their efforts produce no lasting success.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 129:8 states that people passing by bless the enemies of Zion in the name of the LORD.
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:8 says neither do those who pass by say, 'The blessing of the LORD be upon you,' indicating that the enemies are not blessed or greeted with favor.

questions.question: How does Psalms 129:5 teach about humility and prayer in the face of opposition?
options: It encourages believers to retaliate aggressively
It calls for believers to pray for the confounding and turning back of those who hate Zion
It teaches to ignore enemies completely
It advises to seek revenge personally
questions.correctAnswer: It calls for believers to pray for the confounding and turning back of those who hate Zion
questions.explanation: Verse 5 is a prayer asking God to confound and turn back those who hate Zion, showing the biblical virtue of relying on God through prayer rather than personal vengeance.

questions.question: What does the imagery of plowers plowing upon the psalmist’s back in Psalms 129:3 teach about enduring suffering?
options: Suffering will always overcome the believer
The psalmist endured affliction yet was not overcome
Affliction is a sign of God’s displeasure
One should avoid suffering at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist endured affliction yet was not overcome
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes harsh suffering, but paired with verse 2, which says they have not prevailed, it teaches endurance through hardship by trusting God.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 129:2 and 129:4, how does faith in God empower believers facing adversity?
options: Faith in God causes believers to ignore problems
Faith in God assures believers that adversaries cannot ultimately prevail because God breaks their power
Faith in God guarantees a life without problems
Faith in God means avoiding conflict at all costs
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God assures believers that adversaries cannot ultimately prevail because God breaks their power
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states enemies have not prevailed despite affliction, and verse 4 explains God cuts the cords of the wicked, encouraging believers to trust God's deliverance.

questions.question: What is the significance of the grass withering before it grows in Psalms 129:6 for Christian living?
options: It shows the importance of patience in growth
It symbolizes the fleeting nature of ungodly plans and opposition
It encourages believers to focus on material gain
It teaches that all things will flourish without effort
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the fleeting nature of ungodly plans and opposition
questions.explanation: The grass that withers before it grows (verse 6) illustrates how the plans of those who oppose God's people will fail, encouraging believers to trust in God's justice and timing.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 129:1 suggests that affliction from youth is a shared experience among Israel.
questions.explanation: Verse 1 invites Israel to acknowledge that many times affliction has occurred from youth, indicating a communal experience of hardship.

questions.question: How does the contrast between the enemies’ failure to harvest in Psalms 129:7 and the psalmist’s endurance teach about perseverance?
options: It teaches that enemies will ultimately succeed
It shows that perseverance leads to fruitful outcomes while opposition fades
It suggests giving up when faced with opposition
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that perseverance leads to fruitful outcomes while opposition fades
questions.explanation: Verse 7 indicates the enemies' labor is fruitless, while the psalmist’s endurance and God’s intervention (verses 2 and 4) show that faithfulness leads to lasting success.

questions.question: What does Psalms 129:8 imply about the social consequences for those who oppose God’s people?
options: They are welcomed and blessed by passersby
They receive no blessing or greeting from those who pass by
They become leaders in the community
questions.correctAnswer: They receive no blessing or greeting from those who pass by
questions.explanation: Verse 8 explains that those who go by do not say blessings in the LORD’s name to the enemies, illustrating social rejection as part of their downfall.

questions.question: What does Psalms 129:5-6 teach about God’s protection over Zion and the fate of its enemies?
options: Enemies will be confounded and become like withered grass
questions.correctAnswer: Enemies will be confounded and become like withered grass
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 together show that those who hate Zion will be confounded and turned back, becoming as grass on housetops which wither before growing, symbolizing their defeat.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 129:3 describes the enemies’ actions as gentle and kind.
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes enemies as plowers who plowed upon the psalmist’s back and made long their furrows, indicating harsh and painful treatment, not gentleness.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 129 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 129.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand' in Psalms 129:7 metaphorically suggest?
options: The mower gains no profit from the grass cut
The mower is overwhelmed with abundance
The mower's hand is full of blessings
questions.correctAnswer: The mower gains no profit from the grass cut
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:7 uses this metaphor to describe how the efforts of the enemies yield no benefit, as the mower does not fill his hand with grass, indicating no gain.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'nor he that bindeth sheaves his bosom' in the context of Psalms 129:7?
options: It depicts the futility of enemies' efforts
It celebrates the harvest of blessings
It signifies the gathering of Israel
It refers to a joyful festival
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts the futility of enemies' efforts
questions.explanation: The phrase in Psalms 129:7 shows that those who bind sheaves find no reward, symbolizing the failure of the enemies' attempts against Israel.

questions.question: According to Psalms 129:8, what do the passersby refrain from saying to those who hate Zion?
options: The blessing of the LORD be upon you
questions.correctAnswer: The blessing of the LORD be upon you
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:8 states that those passing by do not say, 'The blessing of the LORD be upon you,' to the enemies of Zion, indicating a lack of blessing or goodwill.

questions.question: Which earlier Psalm shares a thematic connection with Psalms 129 regarding the deliverance of Israel from enemies?
questions.explanation: Psalm 126 also reflects on Israel's restoration and deliverance from affliction, connecting thematically with Psalms 129's focus on affliction and divine rescue (Psalms 129:1-8 and Psalm 126).

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'afflicted' in Psalms 129:1?
options: To be pressed down or oppressed
questions.correctAnswer: To be pressed down or oppressed
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word used for 'afflicted' in Psalms 129:1 is from the root עָנָה (anah), meaning to be pressed down or oppressed, reflecting the suffering endured from youth.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of enemies' efforts being in vain as seen in Psalms 129:7-8?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:31's declaration 'If God be for us, who can be against us?' echoes Psalms 129:7-8's theme of enemies ultimately failing against God's people.

questions.question: What literary device is predominantly used in Psalms 129:6-7 to describe the fate of those who hate Zion?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:6-7 uses similes comparing enemies to grass on rooftops that withers before growth, illustrating their fleeting and fruitless existence.

questions.question: According to Psalms 129:4, what has the LORD done to the 'cords of the wicked'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:4 states that the LORD, being righteous, has cut asunder the cords of the wicked, symbolizing the breaking of their power.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 129:5 calls for those who hate Zion to be honored and blessed.
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:5 actually calls for those who hate Zion to be confounded and turned back, not honored or blessed.

questions.question: True or False: The metaphor of plowers making long furrows on the psalmist's back in Psalms 129:3 suggests deep and repeated suffering.
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:3 uses the imagery of plowers making long furrows on the back to express the extent and severity of the affliction experienced from youth.

questions.question: In Psalms 129:2, despite many afflictions from youth, what is the outcome regarding the enemies' success?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:2 clearly states that although afflicted many times, the enemies have not prevailed against the psalmist.

questions.question: How does the theme of divine justice in Psalms 129:4 relate to the covenantal promises found in Deuteronomy 28?
options: It reflects God’s intervention to break the power of the wicked as part of blessings for obedience
It contradicts the blessings and curses of Deuteronomy
It emphasizes human effort over divine action
It focuses on foreign nations' prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects God’s intervention to break the power of the wicked as part of blessings for obedience
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:4’s depiction of God cutting asunder the cords of the wicked aligns with Deuteronomy 28's promises where God acts to protect and bless Israel by defeating enemies.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a similar expression of enemies being like grass that withers, as found in Psalms 129:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:7 uses the imagery of grass that withers quickly, similar to Psalms 129:6, to represent the fleeting nature of human life and enemies.

questions.question: What purpose does the phrase 'Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth' in Psalms 129:1 serve in the structure of this psalm?
options: It serves as an inclusio framing the psalm
It is a prophecy of future events
It is a refrain from another psalm
questions.correctAnswer: It serves as an inclusio framing the psalm
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase in Psalms 129:1 and 129:2 acts as an inclusio, a literary device framing the psalm’s theme of enduring affliction yet prevailing.

questions.question: What is the original audience's likely understanding of the 'blessing of the LORD' mentioned in Psalms 129:8?
options: A divine favor and peace upon God's people
questions.correctAnswer: A divine favor and peace upon God's people
questions.explanation: The original audience would recognize 'blessing of the LORD' in Psalms 129:8 as God's favor and peace, a common theme in Israelite prayers and blessings.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 129 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 129 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 129 teach about the afflictions faced by Israel?
options: They were only afflicted in their old age
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:1 states, 'Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Israel now say:' This indicates that Israel has faced numerous afflictions throughout their history.

questions.question: According to Psalms 129, what has been the outcome of the afflictions faced by Israel?
options: They have not prevailed against Israel
They have led to their exile
questions.correctAnswer: They have not prevailed against Israel
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:2 affirms, 'yet they have not prevailed against me,' showing that despite the afflictions, Israel has remained resilient.

questions.question: What does the imagery of the plowers in Psalms 129 symbolize?
questions.explanation: The imagery in Psalms 129:3, 'The plowers plowed upon my back: they made long their furrows,' symbolizes the deep suffering and oppression Israel has faced.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Psalms 129:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:4 states, 'The LORD is righteous: he hath cut asunder the cords of the wicked.' This highlights God's justice in dealing with evil.

questions.question: What is the prayer for those who hate Zion in Psalms 129:5?
options: Let them be confounded and turned back
questions.correctAnswer: Let them be confounded and turned back
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:5 requests, 'Let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Zion,' indicating a desire for justice against adversaries.

questions.question: What metaphor is used to describe those who oppose Zion in Psalms 129:6?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:6 compares adversaries to 'the grass upon the housetops, which withereth afore it groweth up,' signifying their lack of permanence.

questions.question: What does Psalms 129:7 convey about the fate of the wicked?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:7 states, 'Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand; nor he that bindeth sheaves his bosom,' indicating that the wicked will not reap benefits.

questions.question: What blessing is omitted for those who go by the wicked according to Psalms 129:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:8 notes, 'Neither do they which go by say, The blessing of the LORD be upon you,' emphasizing the absence of divine favor for the wicked.

questions.question: What overarching theme is portrayed throughout Psalms 129 regarding Israel's suffering?
questions.explanation: The chapter illustrates Israel's resilience through affliction and God's justice in delivering them from their enemies, showcasing a hopeful narrative.

questions.question: How does Psalms 129 fit into the larger narrative of redemption in Scripture?
options: It shows God's favor without suffering
It highlights the necessity of suffering for growth
It promotes a life without conflict
It denies the reality of evil
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the necessity of suffering for growth
questions.explanation: Psalms 129 underscores that suffering is a part of Israel's journey, leading to divine justice and resilience, fitting within the broader redemptive arc.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'cut asunder the cords of the wicked' in Psalms 129:4 imply about God's actions?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'cut asunder the cords of the wicked' signifies God's active intervention against evil, demonstrating His righteousness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 129 reveal about the relationship between Israel and their enemies?
questions.explanation: The chapter reflects that despite afflictions, Israel's enemies will not prevail and will ultimately face God's justice.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the blessing of the LORD' indicate in the context of Psalms 129:8?
questions.explanation: The absence of 'the blessing of the LORD' for the wicked in Psalms 129:8 signifies that they are outside of God's favor and protection.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5 and 6 convey about the fate of those who hate Zion?
options: They will be confused and wither
questions.correctAnswer: They will be confused and wither
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 combine to show that those who hate Zion will face confusion and a lack of growth, symbolized by the withering grass.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not intervene in human suffering. What does Psalms 129:4-5 actually teach?
options: God actively cuts the cords of the wicked
God allows all suffering to continue
questions.correctAnswer: God actively cuts the cords of the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 129:4-5 reveals that God is engaged and righteous, actively intervening against the wicked, contrary to the sceptics' claim.
